question_text:
Premise 1: All department heads are career service eligible.
Premise 2: Mr. Reyes is a department head.
Conclusion: Therefore, Mr. Reyes is career service eligible.
This is an example of:

hint_ladder.title: Structure ng Argumento
hint_ladder.text: Pansinin ang flow: general rule, specific person, certain conclusion. Deductive ang pattern, hindi hula.

hint_ladder.title: Kung-Then na Relasyon
hint_ladder.text: 'Kung department head, eligible.' Si Reyes ay dept head, so eligible. Affirm ang first part (antecedent) para makuha ang second.

hint_ladder.title: Ibang Patterns
hint_ladder.text: Modus Tollens: 'Kung P then Q. Hindi Q, so hindi P.' Hindi iyan dito. Valid ito, hindi fallacy. Inductive ay probability lang.

hint_ladder.title: Pangalan ng Pattern
hint_ladder.text: Modus Ponens: affirm P (antecedent) to conclude Q (consequent). Kung P then Q, P totoo, Q totoo. 'Ponens = positive affirmation.'

A.text: You might have chosen A because Modus Tollens denies the consequent, not affirms the antecedent like here.

B.text: Correct. This is Modus Ponens: affirming the antecedent (P) leads to the consequent (Q).

C.text: You might have chosen C because you thought it's invalid, but the argument is valid—if premises true, conclusion must be true.

D.text: You might have chosen D because it seems like a general rule, but inductive reasoning only gives probability, not certainty.

next_time_rule: Tandaan: Ponens = Positive affirmation (P totoo, Q totoo). Tollens = Take away (di Q totoo, di P totoo).
deconstruct_text:
Imagine a barangay budget scenario: 'All barangay captains must attend the meeting.' Kapitan Reyes is a captain, so he must attend. That's Modus Ponens: a general rule applied to a specific person to yield a guaranteed conclusion. It's deductive, not just probable.

The logical structure is: If P (department head) then Q (eligible). Here, P is true (Mr. Reyes is a dept. head), so Q must be true. This is affirming the antecedent. Compare with Modus Tollens: If P then Q, but Q is false, so P false. That's denial of the consequent.

Taglish memory trick: 'Ponens' parang 'positive affirmation' – sinasabi mong totoo ang P, kaya totoo rin ang Q. 'Tollens' parang 'taking away' – inaalis mo ang Q, kaya mawawala rin ang P. Sa exam, tignan mo kung ina-affirm ang unang part o dini-deny ang second part.

Sa problemang ito, klaro na ina-affirm natin ang antecedent (Mr. Reyes ay department head) para i-conclude ang consequent (eligible siya). Walang fallacy, at hindi ito induction dahil certain ang conclusion, hindi probable.
